newsitem.title: CROATIA: Rebel Moslem warlord slams Izetbegovic as Stalinist.
newsitem.headline: Rebel Moslem warlord slams Izetbegovic as Stalinist.

text.p: Deposed Moslem warlord Fikret Abdic, indicted for armed rebellion by the Bosnian government, on Thursday accused President Alija Izetbegovic and his ruling SDA party of using Stalinist methods to curb the opposition.

A court in the northwest town of Bihac, Abdic's former stronghold, is currently trying the rebel leader in absentia for allegedly detaining civilians, blocking relief aid and shelling the town's mostly Moslem population from 1993-1995.

"My real prosecutor is (Bosnian president) Alija Izetbegovic," Abdic told a news conference in the Croatian capital of Zagreb. "With this trial he has proven to be a good disciple of the Stalinist school."

Abdic, who has registered a political party named Democratic People's Union (DNZ) to contest Bosnia's post-war elections, said the authorities had deliberately launched the trial less than two weeks before the September 14 poll.
"The SDA is trying to convict me ten days ahead of elections and thus influence the will of the people," he said.
Since registering the DNZ in the southwest Bosnian town of Mostar, Abdic has held no pre-election rallies and not shown up once in Moslem-controlled areas, where he could be arrested.
"We're a legally registered party working in illegal conditions," he said.

The Organisation for Cooperation and Security in Europe, which is in charge of organising and monitoring the election, has allowed the DNZ to compete and Abdic to run for president. "This proves we're not war criminals," he said.
But Abdic accused Bosnian government authorities of trying to push him out of the picture by not allowing him to appear on state-run television.
"We haven't been given the basic rights - freedom of movement and media campaigning," he said.
Abdic, a businessman-turned-politician and an arch rival of Izetbegovic, led a rebellion against the Sarajevo government in 1993 and declared the Bihac enclave "an autonomous region".
He armed his troops by reaching deals with Croat and Serb armies fighting the government. Sarajevo's forces recaptured the enclave in 1995 and Abdic fled with his followers to Croatia.
Many of them have since returned to the region and observers have reported numerous cases of harassment by pro-government compatriots.

"You ask why the SDA is being repressive against DNZ only? Because we are the only real opposition party in Bosnia," Abdic said. "But for their repression, the SDA would suffer a terrible defeat in the election."
